<meta>This page provides a detailed bibliographic and historical description of a bilingual Greek and Armenian manuscript, identified as Manuscript 9 in the Armenian collection. It includes notes from several scholars, including the 19th-century Orientalist Édouard Dulaurier.</meta>

<insert>
* [Armenian, 9.] <note>original: "Arménien, 9"</note> Acts of the Apostles, Catholic Epistles, Pauline Epistles, and Revelation; damaged at the beginning and end (Greek-Armenian).
12th century. Parchment. 323 leaves. (Bigot.—De Mesmes.—Reg. 2247, 2.) M.
</insert>

A parchment codex in folio size, written in a very skilled hand among those to be listed, damaged at the beginning and the end, containing:
1. The Acts of the Apostles along with an Armenian interpretation <note>i.e., translation</note>, with one page following the received Greek text and the other the Armenian version; it appears to be by the same hand.
2. The Catholic Epistles with the same Armenian interpretation, with an Italian translation <note>original: "italica conversione"</note> added to the margin, which was likely composed by one of those Sicilians living in the East.
3. The Pauline Epistles, with both interpretations separated.
4. The Revelation <note>original: "Apocalypsis"</note> with the same interpretations.
Prefaced to almost every <unclear>section</unclear> <unclear>fourth</unclear> <unclear>flower</unclear> are prologues and arguments for the Acts, the Catholic Epistles of the Apostles, and the Pauline Epistles.

This manuscript codex is to be considered most precious, as it was written by the hand of Saint Nerses of Lampron <note>A 12th-century Armenian archbishop of Tarsus known for his scholarship and efforts to unite the Armenian and Latin churches.</note> in Cilicia, the second bishop of the city of Tarsus, as is shown by the Armenian <note>original: "armeniacus"</note> testimony, and is evident from the note which appears on page 13 <unclear>discussed</unclear>. Folio 294 verso.
St. Nerses was born 1153 AD and died in 1198.
Édouard Dulaurier, Year 1840

### The Manifestation of Light and the Body

Because this was not [spoken] <unclear>at all</unclear> with boldness <note>original: "παρρησίας" (parrhesias) — a Greek term for "bold speech" or "candidness," often used in the New Testament to describe the apostles' preaching.</note> to all the world. Because everything in the world happens in darkness and the evil is reproved by the light; for this reason he established a cause <unclear>made</unclear> instead of the seventeen <note>This "seventeen" may refer to a specific group of martyrs or a numerical symbolism in the original text.</note> who were constrained, and this consisted in him for whose sake [it was]. And being whole of body, confessing death with boldness
<margin>Father</margin> they were [tried] among stones <note>Likely a reference to stoning, a common form of martyrdom.</note> <unclear>being troubled</unclear> by the judgment of injustice in the life and death of the saints, according to him their own reproof exists. But also for those in a common body, and in the suffering to come from the fitting immortal one, the gods <note>original: "οἱ θεοὶ" (hoi theoi); here possibly referring to divine beings or a specific pagan context being addressed.</note> in fear of the one who loves, of the <term>Lord</term> <note>original: "Θυ" (Theou) — a common abbreviation in Greek manuscripts for "of God."</note> by the grace of God, becoming and through God himself; for he does not exist as a mind for them. Because also according to the <unclear>duration of time</unclear> in his own body. The powers of the ephemeral consisted of the ancestral powers and through those things outside the body, contained because it is being fulfilled according to the whole.

<column-break/>

For this [was spoken] with such boldness <note>Armenian: "քաջութեամբ" (k'ajut'eamb) — literally "with bravery," used here to translate the Greek "parrhesia."</note> for everyone to see entirely, speaking by the laws before the world. For everything that is in this world is of darkness and is evil, and it is revealed by that light; for that reason he gave causes instead of various others. And while they stood with such courage, and revealing his goodness through other things which he brought as a manifest testimony, confessing death at once to the dead and the living, [having been] openly stoned from all sides. Furthermore, they made his goodness suffer by means of death, which they considered to be for their own mortality in such evil. But also for those who received the sufferings in the common body, in total weakness, there is reconciliation by divine grace. And confessing to all both that which would come from him and that which lay before them, so that according to the time it might be revealed in his own body. Giving powers greater than the heavenly powers and the manifest service allotted to the body; because from him, and in the midst, and among all, his illumination is mixed and opened so that it becomes such a victory.

<summary>This page presents a bilingual Greek-Armenian discourse on the spiritual struggle between light and darkness, emphasizing the "boldness" of the saints who confess their faith despite persecution and stoning. It explores the theological concept of divine grace being revealed through the physical body and the ultimate victory of light over worldly evil.</summary>

# Acts of the Apostles - Chapter 13

For David, after he had served his own generation <note>original Greek: "ἰδίᾳ γενεὰν"; Armenian: "յազգի անդ իւրում" — referring to his lifetime of service</note> by the will of God, fell asleep, and was laid with his fathers, and saw corruption <note>term: corruption; refers to the physical decay of the body after death</note>. But He whom God raised up did not see corruption. Therefore, let it be known to you, brothers, that through Him the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you; and from all things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses, by Him everyone who believes is justified.

--- Page 49 ---
<meta>This page continues the narrative of the Acts of the Apostles, chapter 19. The previous page (3) described Paul’s arrival in Ephesus and his interaction with the disciples of John the Baptist. On this page, the text transitions to the miracles performed by Paul and the failed attempt by Jewish exorcists to mimic his power, followed by the growth of the church in Ephesus and Paul's future travel plans.</meta>

# Page 46

<warning>Slight blurring at the page edges and gutter; some text near the center fold is difficult to read but reconstructed from biblical context (Acts 19:11-22).</warning>

And God performed no ordinary miracles <note>original Greek: δυνάμεις οὐ τὰς τυχούσας, literally "not the ordinary powers"</note> by the hands of Paul. So that even handkerchiefs <note>original Greek: σουδάρια (soudaria), a Latin loanword for a sweat-cloth or face-cloth</note> or aprons <note>original Greek: σιμικίνθια (simikinthia), a workman's apron</note> were carried from his skin to those who were sick, and the diseases left them, and the evil spirits went out. 

But some of the itinerant Jewish exorcists also attempted to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, “I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul preaches.” 

Now there were seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish high priest, who were doing this. But the evil spirit answered and said to them, “Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize; but who are you?” 

And the man in whom the evil spirit lived leaped upon them, and having overpowered both of them <note>The Greek text here uses ἀμφοτέρων (amphoterōn), meaning "both," though seven sons were mentioned previously; this is a known detail in early manuscripts</note>, he prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

<column-break/>

And God performed no small miracles by the hand of Paul’s hands. So that they carried from his sweat <note>The Armenian specifies "from his sweat" (i krtnēn) where the Greek says "from his skin."</note> handkerchiefs or veils <note>original Armenian: վարշամակս (varshamaks)</note> to the sick, and their diseases were healed, and the evil spirits left them.

Some of the traveling Jewish exorcists dared to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus Christ over those who had these evil spirits and said, “I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.” 

There were seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish high priest, who were doing this. The evil spirit gave an answer and said, “Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize. Who are you?” 

And the man in whom the evil spirit lived rushed at them. He seized them and the two of them <note>original Armenian: զերկոսին (zerkosin). Like the Greek, the Armenian specifies "the two," suggesting only two of the seven sons were involved in this specific encounter.</note>, and he defeated them, so that they fled from that house naked and wounded.

---

# 46

This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified. 

And many of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds. And a good number of those who practiced magic arts <note>original Greek: τὰ περίεργα, literally "the curious things," referring to the occult</note> brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. And they counted up the value of them and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver <note>This was a massive sum, equivalent to the daily wages of 50,000 laborers.</note>. 

So the word of the Lord grew mightily and prevailed. 

When these things were fulfilled, Paul purposed in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after passing through Macedonia and Achaia, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.” And having sent into Macedonia two of those who ministered to him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a time.

<column-break/>

And this became known to all the Jews and heathens <note>original Armenian: հեթանոսաց (het’anosats), often used for Greeks or Gentiles</note> who lived in Ephesus. And fear fell upon all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified. 

And many of those who believed came to confess and tell of their deeds. 

<margin>჻</margin> And many of those who practiced the arts of sorcery <note>original Armenian: կախարդութեան (kakhardut’ean)</note> brought their books and burned them before everyone. And they calculated their price and found it to be five myriad <note>A "myriad" is ten thousand; five myriads equals 50,000.</note> pieces of silver. 

And in this way, the word of the Lord grew and became strong. 

As this was completed, Paul set in his mind <note>original Armenian: եդ... ի մտի (ed... i mti), literally "placed in his mind"</note> to travel through Macedonia and Achaia and to go to Jerusalem. And he said, “After I go there, I must also see Rome.” 

He sent to Macedonia two of his ministers, Timothy and Erastus, and he himself stayed for some time in Asia.

<summary>This page describes Paul's successful ministry in Ephesus, where even items touched by him healed the sick, and the subsequent failure of Sceva's sons to imitate his exorcisms. It records the widespread conversion of the city, the public burning of expensive magic books, and Paul's plan to visit Jerusalem and Rome.</summary>

# Page 47

About that time, there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way <note>original: τῆς ὁδοῦ (tēs hodou) / ճանապարհին (janaparhin). "The Way" was one of the earliest names for the Christian movement</note>. For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis <note>original: ἀρτέμιδος / Արտեմեայ. Artemis (often called Diana by the Romans) was the patron goddess of Ephesus; her temple there was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World</note>, provided no little work for the craftsmen. Having gathered these together, along with those in similar trades, he said, "Men, you know that from this business comes our prosperity. And you see and hear that not only in Ephesus but in almost all of Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable crowd, saying that gods made by hands are not gods. Not only is there danger that this trade of ours may fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and her majesty—whom all Asia and the world worship—will be stripped of her greatness." When they heard this and were filled with rage, they cried out, saying, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

<column-break/>

And it happened at that time that there was no small stir concerning the Way. For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, used to make silver shrines for Artemis, and he gave the craftsmen no small profit. Having gathered these and others of such trades together, he said: "Men, you know that our profit is from this work. And you see and hear that not only for the Ephesians, but for almost all of the Asians, this Paul has made a change in many people, turning them away by saying that those made by hands are not gods. And not only does this matter risk bringing us into danger in our trade, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be considered as nothing, whom all Asia and the whole world worship." When they heard this, they were full of anger and cried out, saying, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

---

And the whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed together into the theater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul’s travel companions. But when Paul wanted to enter among the crowd <note>original: τὸν δῆμον (ton dēmon), referring to the citizen body or assembly</note>, the disciples would not let him. And even some of the Asiarchs <note>original: ἀσιαρχῶν (asiarchōn) / յասիապետացն (asiapetats’n). These were high-ranking provincial officials who presided over public games and religious festivals</note>, who were his friends, sent word to him and urged him not to venture into the theater. Now some were shouting one thing and some another, for the assembly <note>original: ἐκκλησία (ekklēsia). In a Greek context, this refers to a legal political assembly, though it later became the word for "church"</note> was in confusion, and the majority did not know why they had come together. From the crowd, they brought forward Alexander, whom the Jews had pushed forward. And Alexander, gesturing with his hand, wanted to make a defense to the crowd. But when they recognized that he was a Jew, a single voice came from them all as they shouted for about two hours, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" After the city clerk <note>original: ὁ γραμματεὺς (ho grammateus), the highest-ranking local official responsible for the city's archives and public meetings</note> had quieted the crowd, he said, "Men of Ephesus..."

<column-break/>

And the city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater. They seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were companions of Paul. But when Paul wanted to enter into the assembly of the people, the disciples did not allow him. And some of the Asiarchs who were his friends sent word to him and pleaded that he would not give himself up to the theater. Some were shouting one thing and others another, for the assembly was confused, and many did not know for what reason they had gathered. And from the crowd they brought forward Alexander, and as the Jews pushed him forward, Alexander moved his hand and wanted to give an answer to the crowd. But when they knew that the man was a Jew, a single cry came from everyone for about two hours, shouting, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" The city clerk silenced the crowd and said, "Men of Ephesus..."

When two years had passed, Felix <note>original: Φῆλιξ (Phēlix); Antonius Felix, the Roman procurator who had kept Paul in prison hoping for a bribe.</note> was succeeded by Porcius Festus. Because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.

Festus, therefore, having arrived in the province, went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea after three days. The chief priests and the leading men of the Jews appeared before him to present their case against Paul. They urged him, asking for a favor against Paul: that Festus might have him brought to Jerusalem. They were planning an ambush to kill him on the road.

Festus, however, answered that Paul was being kept in Caesarea and that he himself was about to go there shortly. "So," he said, "let those among you who have authority go down with me. If there is anything wrong with the man, let them accuse him."

And when two years were completed, Porcius Festus became the successor to Felix. And because Felix wished to do a favor for the Jews, he left Paul bound.

When Festus arrived in the province <note>original: յիշխանութիւնն (yishkhanut‘iunn); literally "into the authority" or "the government."</note>, after three days he went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea. They were planning an ambush to kill him on the road.

But Festus gave an answer: that Paul was being kept in Caesarea, and that he himself would be going there soon. "Those of you who are capable," he said, "let them go down with me, and if there is any fault in the man, let them bring charges against him."

judgment seat <note>original: βήματος (bēmatos); the official tribunal or raised platform from which a Roman magistrate delivered legal rulings.</note>, he ordered Paul to be brought in. Paul defended himself, saying, "I have committed no offense, neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar."

As free men, not as those who have freedom as a cloak for malice, but as the servants of God. Honor all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.

Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and the temperate, but also to the untrained <note>original: "non amaestrati," meaning those who are harsh or lack proper conduct</note>. For this is a great [grace] if for conscience toward God one endures sorrow, suffering unjustly. For what great appearance is it if you, sinning...

<column-break/>

so that in the thing in which they speak against you as evildoers, they may, by observing your good works, glorify God in the day of visitation. Be subject therefore to every human creation for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as supreme, or to governors as those sent through him for the vengeance of evildoers and the praise of those who do good. For so is the will of God, that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.

As free men, and not having freedom as a covering for wickedness, but as servants of God. Honor all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honor the king.

<column-break/>

they might slander you as evildoers, that by observing your good works they may glorify God in the day of visitation. Be subject to every human creature for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as superior, or to judges as those sent by him for the vengeance of evildoers and the praise of those who do good. For such is the will of God, that by doing good you silence the ignorance of foolish men. As free men, and not having your freedom as a cloak for evil, but as servants of God. Honor all men, love the brotherhood, fear God, honor the kings.

Servants, be subject with all fear to your masters, not only to the good and the gentle, but also to the stubborn. For this is grace, if for the sake of a good conscience one endures sorrow and suffers grief unjustly. For what merit is there if when you sin and are punished you endure it? But if for doing good...

and being buffeted you shall endure? But if doing good and suffering you shall endure, this is grace before God. For unto this were you called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving behind for you an example <note>original: "hypogrammon," literally a writing-copy for students to trace</note> so that you should follow in his footsteps; who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth; who being reviled, did not revile in return; suffering, he did not threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously; who his own self bore our sins in his body on the tree <note>original: "xylon," meaning the wood of the cross</note>, so that having died to sins we might live to righteousness; by whose stripe you were healed. Who when slandered did not slander in return; suffering, he did not threaten, but gave himself to the righteous judge. Who himself lifted our sins in his body onto the wood of the cross <note>original: "khach'ap'aytn"</note>, so that we might be free from those sins and live for righteousness; by whose wounds you were healed. For you were like wandering sheep, but now have returned to the shepherd and overseer <note>original: "tesuch," the equivalent of "bishop"</note> of your souls. <column-break/>

For to this you were called, because Christ has suffered for you, leaving you an example, so that you should follow his steps; who did no sin, nor in his mouth was found deceit; who when he was reviled, did not revile; and when he suffered, he did not threaten, but gave himself to him who judged him wrongly <note>Note: The Italian translator uses "torto" (wrongly), whereas the Greek and Armenian emphasize God's "righteous" judgment.</note>. Without discord, likewise, be subject with your conduct. The adornment <note>original: "capellatura," referring to hairstyles or head-dress</note> of which should not be the outward display of braids or the adornment of covering of clothes—but let it be the person in the heart, hidden with the incorruptible sweetness and of a quiet spirit, which is precious <note>original: "e' ridio," likely a corruption of "e' pretioso"</note> in the sight of God. For in this way the holy women <note>original: "le sante femine," likely what "lefante femine" in the OCR intended</note> of old adorned themselves, being submissive to their own husbands.

Just as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord; of whom you have become daughters <note>original: "figlioli," though referring to daughters in context</note> by doing good and not fearing any disturbance.

Similarly, you husbands, dwelling together with them according to knowledge, give honor to the woman as to the weaker vessel—since you are together heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers are not hindered. Finally, be all of one mind—together lovers of the brotherhood, merciful.

<column-break/>

<margin>3 / 1</margin>
Likewise, wives, being subject to your own husbands, so that even if some are disobedient to the word, they may be won over without a word through the conduct of the wives, having observed your pure conduct in fear. Let your adornment not be the external braiding of hair and putting on of gold or wearing of fine clothes; but the hidden person of the heart, in the incorruptible [beauty] of a quiet and gentle spirit, which is very precious before God. Husbands likewise, dwelling together according to knowledge as with a weaker female vessel, assigning honor, as also being joint-heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.

Similarly also let wives be subject to their own husbands; so that even if there are some who are rebellious to the word, they may be won by the wordless conduct of the wives, having seen your holy conduct in fear. Whose [adornment] should not be the external braiding of hair and the wrapping around of gold, or the ornament of fine clothing. But the hidden person of the heart, with the incorruptibility of meekness and a quiet spirit, which is manifold <note>original: "բազմապատիկ," meaning manifold or abundant</note> before God. Of whom you have become children of good works, and not of those troubled by any fear. Similarly also let men dwell with them with wisdom, as with a weak vessel, giving honor to wives as companions of the grace of life, so that there be no obstacle to your prayers.

And finally, all be like-minded, sympathetic, brother-loving, tenderhearted, humble-minded; not returning evil for evil or insult for insult; but on the contrary blessing, knowing that to this you were called, that you might inherit a blessing. For he who wants that which we have of life—to see good times—let him restrain his tongue from evil and his lips so they do not speak deceit; but let him depart from evil and do good; let him ask for peace and follow it—for the eyes of the Lord are upon the just and his ears are upon their prayers; but the countenance of the Lord is upon evildoers. But let their fear not move you, nor be troubled—but sanctify the Lord Christ <note>original: "xpō," abbreviation for Christo</note> in your hearts. Always be prepared for a response to every man who asks you for a reason for that [hope].

# THE SECOND LETTER OF PETER
# THE SECOND CATHOLIC [LETTER]
Simeon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ: to those who have equally obtained with us the lot of precious faith in the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ: Grace be with you and may peace be multiplied through the knowledge of God and of Jesus Christ our Lord. As His divine power has granted us all things for life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and virtue. By which precious and great promises are granted to us.

<column-break/>

# Page 149

->**On the Nature of the Divine and the Created Order**<-

It is necessary to consider that the first cause <note>original: "causa prima," a common philosophical term for God</note> is not merely a mover of the heavens, but the very source of all being. As the ancient philosophers have noted, nothing comes from nothing, yet the divine intellect brings forth the forms of all things through a single act of will.

<margin>The soul is the mirror of the cosmos.</margin>

We must distinguish between the *eternal* and the *temporal*. While the body is subject to the laws of decay and change, the intellective soul <note>The part of the human soul capable of rational thought and understanding universal truths</note> participates in a light that does not fade. This is what the Greeks called the *Logos* <note>original: "Λόγος," meaning Word, Reason, or Plan</note>, which serves as the bridge between the hidden God and the visible world.

<column-break/>

### The Hierarchy of Being

| Level of Being | Characteristic | Nature |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Divine | Immutable | Pure Actuality |
| Celestial | Persistent | Moving but incorruptible |
| Terrestrial | Transient | Subject to generation and decay |

<insert>Note that the elements—earth, air, fire, and water—are but the shadows of these higher realities.</insert>

Therefore, when we speak of "justice" or "beauty" in this world, we are merely using <gloss>imperfect</gloss> names for that which exists in perfection within the divine mind. As it is written in the sacred texts: "The heavens declare the glory of God" <note>original: "Coeli enarrant gloriam Dei," quoting Psalm 19:1</note>. This declaration is not made with a human voice, but through the very harmony of the spheres <note>The ancient theory that the movements of celestial bodies create a divine music or mathematical proportion</note>.

We conclude this section by affirming that the study of the natural world is, in truth, a form of worship, provided the mind looks beyond the <unclear>material</unclear> surface to the spiritual depths beneath.

<summary>This page explores the philosophical relationship between the divine first cause and the physical world, utilizing a hierarchy of being to explain how earthly forms reflect divine perfections. It emphasizes the role of the rational soul and the "Logos" as intermediaries in understanding the cosmos.</summary>

<keywords>First Cause, Hierarchy of Being, Logos, Soul, Divine Intellect, Harmony of the Spheres, Metaphysics</keywords>

# Epistle to the Galatians, Chapters 2 and 3

Yet knowing that we are justified by the faith of Christ our Lord <note>original Italian: "fede di Xp̃o n. s̃."; Greek: "πιστεως ιησου χριστου"</note> and not by the works of the law: For no flesh shall be justified in the works of the law. If we ourselves, seeking to be justified in Christ, are found to be sinners, is Christ then a minister of sin? By no means! For if I rebuild those things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor <note>original Italian: "faccio me p̃ uaricante"; Greek: "παραβατην εμαυτον συνιστανω"</note>. For I through the law am dead to the law, so that I may live to God. I was crucified with Christ; I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me. And what I now live in the flesh, I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. I do not cast away the grace of God; for if justice <note>or "righteousness"</note> comes through the law, then Christ died in vain <note>original Italian: "sena cagion"; Armenian: "զուր"</note>.

O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you <note>original Italian: "incantato"; Greek: "εβασκανεν"; Armenian: "նախանձն ատոր արար"</note> not to obey the truth, before whose eyes Christ was condemned and crucified among you? This only I want to learn from you: Did you receive the Holy Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now made perfect by the flesh? Have you suffered so much in vain—if indeed it be in vain?

<column-break/>

Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, unless it be through the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the works of the law; because by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified. But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, is Christ therefore a minister of sin? God forbid. For if I build again these things which I destroyed, I prove myself a transgressor. For I through the law died to the law, that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. I do not nullify the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.

O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you that you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed among you as crucified? This only I want to learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now ending in the flesh? Have you suffered so many things in vain—if it really was in vain?

<column-break/>

We know that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ; and we have believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the works of the law; for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. But if, while we sought to be justified in Christ, we were found to be sinners, then was Christ a minister of sin? Far be it! For the things I tore down, if I build them up again, I show myself a transgressor. For I, through the law, am dead [to it], that I might be established in Christ <note>the Armenian "հաստացեալ" suggests being "established" or "firm" in Him</note>. I am alive, but henceforth not I, but Christ is alive in me. But that which I am now alive in the flesh, [I am] in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. And I do not despise the grace of God. For if righteousness comes forth from the law, then Christ died in vain. O witless Galatians, who has cast an evil eye upon you <note>the Armenian "նախանձն ատոր արար" implies an envious or bewitching look</note>, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was portrayed as given to crucifixion among you? <meta>This page continues the Apostle Paul’s Epistle to the Galatians, specifically focusing on Chapter 3. # The Epistle to the Galatians: Chapter 3

<page-num>43</page-num>

Christ was made a curse <note>original Latin/Italian: "Facto per maledictione Christus"; Greek: "κατάραν"</note> for us; for it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs upon a tree <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 21:23, explaining that Christ’s crucifixion was legally viewed as a "curse" to fulfill and end the Law's penalty</note>. This was done so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. Brothers, I speak in human terms: though it is but a man’s covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no one annuls it or adds to it. Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring <note>original Greek: "σπέρματι"; Armenian: "զաւակ" (seed)</note>. It does not say "and to offsprings," as if to many, but as to one: "And to your offspring," who is Christ. I say this: the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul the covenant previously confirmed by God in Christ, so as to make the promise void. For if the inheritance is from the Law, it is no longer from the promise; but God gave it to Abraham through a promise.

<column-break/>

Knowing that Christ became a curse for us. For it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree. So that the blessing of Abraham might come to the nations <note>original Greek: "ἔθνη" (Gentiles or nations)</note> in Christ Jesus, so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith. Brothers, I speak as a man: no one sets aside or adds to a human covenant once it has been ratified. The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say "and to seeds," as of many, but as of one, "and to your seed," who is Christ. And I say this: the Law, which happened four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul a covenant previously ratified by God in Christ, so as to abolish the promise. For if the inheritance is from the Law, it is no longer from the promise. But God graciously gave it to Abraham through a promise. Why then the Law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom the promise had been made; and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator <note>original Greek: "μεσίτου"</note>.

<column-break/>

And also for our sake, Christ [became] a curse. For it is written: cursed is everyone who hangs from wood <note>original Armenian: "զփայտէ" (wood/tree)</note>. So that the blessing of Abraham might be upon the Gentiles, the blessing of Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Holy Spirit through faith. Brothers, I speak according to humanity; yet no one can despise or command anything more regarding a man's confirmed testament <note>original Armenian: "կտակ" (will or testament)</note>. Now the blessing was promised to Abraham and his offspring. And it does not say "offsprings," as of many, but as of one: "and to your offspring," which is Christ. But I say this: the Law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot abolish the testament previously confirmed by God in Christ, to frustrate the promise. If the blessing was inherited from the Law, then it is no longer from the promise. However, God granted the blessing through the promise. Why then was the Law added? Because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom it was promised; ordained by angels, in the hand of [a mediator].

---

<page-num>44</page-num>

Now a mediator is not for one alone, but God is one. Is the Law then against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that was able to give life, then righteousness <note>or "justification"</note> would indeed have been by the Law. But the Scripture has confined all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe. But before faith came, we were kept under guard by the Law, confined for the faith that was to be revealed. So the Law was our guardian <note>original Greek: "παιδαγωγὸς" (pedagogue), a slave who escorted children to school and supervised their conduct</note> until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith. But after faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian. For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.

<column-break/>

...of a mediator. But a mediator is not a proclaimer for one alone; but God is one. Is the Law then contrary to the promises of God? Heaven forbid! For if a law had been given which was able to make [one] alive, then truly righteousness would have been from that Law. But the scriptures shut everything up under sin, so that the promise through the faith of Jesus Christ might be given to the believers. Before faith came, we were shut up under the Law, guarded for the coming faith which was to be revealed. Henceforth the Law was our tutor <note>original Armenian: "դաստիարակ"</note> unto Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith. But since faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor. For you are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus. For those of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is no distinction of Jew or Gentile, of slave or free, of male or female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus. Then if you are of Jesus Christ, you are therefore Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.

<column-break/>

...a mediator who is not of one [person]: but God is one. The Law, truly, is it against the promises of God? Not at all; it would be impossible for the Law to be able to give life, for truly justice would come from the Law. But the Scripture closed every thing under sin, so that the promise might be given to those who see <note>original Italian: "uedenti" (seers/believers)</note> through the faith of Jesus Christ. Presently in Christ, faith was guarded under the Law, enclosed [until] the faith which was [to come] should manifest itself. Therefore the Law was our discipline <note>original Italian: "disciplina"</note> in Christ, so that we might be made just through faith. But now that faith has come, we are no longer under that discipline. Certainly you are all made sons of God through the faith which [is in] Christ Jesus. For all you who were baptized in Christ have put on Christ. There is no Jew nor Greek, no slave nor free, no male nor female: you are all one, our only one in Christ Jesus. If you are one thing in Christ, then you are the seed of Abraham, heirs according to the promise.

<summary>This page presents the core of Paul's argument in Galatians 3, asserting that the Law of Moses served as a temporary guardian (pedagogue) until Christ arrived. It emphasizes the spiritual equality of all believers—regardless of ethnicity, status, or gender—as heirs to God's promise to Abraham.</summary>

...of the son of the bondwoman. The crown of righteousness; for the son is of the promise. Behold, I **Paul** say to you: if you are circumcised, **Christ** will profit you nothing. I testify to every man who is circumcised, that he is a debtor to perform the whole law. You have been hindered from **Christ**, you who are justified by the law; and you have fallen from grace. For we, through the Spirit, wait for the hope of righteousness from faith. For in **Christ Jesus** neither circumcision is able to do anything, nor uncircumcision; but faith which works through love. You were running well; who stopped you from obeying the truth? For that advice is not from him who called you. A little leaven leavens the whole lump. But I have hope in the Lord concerning you, that you will think nothing else; and he who troubles you shall bear [the judgment].

<column-break/>

...and the image <note>Italian: "effigie" — likeness or representation</note> of the free woman. Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free woman. With which liberty **Christ** has freed us. Stand firm in it, and do not desire to put yourselves again under the yoke of servitude. Behold, I **Paul** say to you: that if you circumcise yourselves, **Christ** will benefit you nothing. And again I testify to every man who circumcises himself, that he is bound to observe the whole law: you shall be separated from **Christ**, you who justify yourselves in the law: you have fallen from grace. We certainly through the spirit expect from faith the hope of justice <note>Italian: "iustitia" — here meaning righteousness or justification</note>: where in **Christ Jesus** neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is of any value: but only faith which works through charity <note>Italian: "carità" — the theological virtue of love (agape)</note>. You were running well: who has impeded you from obeying the truth? This counsel is not from him who has called you. A little leaven corrupts the whole dough. I trust in you in the Lord: that you will have no other knowledge; but he who disturbs you: he shall bear [his judgment].

<summary>This page presents Galatians 5:1-10 in a tri-columnar polyglot format, emphasizing Paul's warning that adopting Jewish circumcision would separate the Galatian converts from the grace of Christ. Paul uses the metaphor of "running a race" and "leaven in dough" to describe how legalism can hinder and corrupt the entire Christian community.</summary>

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus and to the faithful in Christ Jesus: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ, just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless before Him in love, having predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will, to the praise of the glory of His grace, by which He has favored us in the Beloved, in whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of His grace, which He made to abound toward us in all wisdom and prudence. <note>original Greek: "sophia kai phronēsei"</note>

<column-break/>

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus and to the believers in Christ Jesus. Grace be with you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed is God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavens in Christ. As He chose us through Him before the beginning of the world, so that we might be holy and spotless before Him in love. He predestined us beforehand for adoption <note>literally "son-ship"</note> through Jesus Christ into the same, according to the pleasure of His will; for the praise of the glory of His grace, by which He made us joyful through His Beloved. By whom we have salvation <note>original Armenian: "p'rkut'iwn," meaning salvation or redemption</note> through His blood, the forgiveness of our sins, according to the greatness of His grace, which abounded in us with all wisdom and knowledge.

## To Philemon

Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved friend and fellow laborer, and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers, hearing of your love and the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints; so that the sharing of your faith may become effective by the acknowledgment of every good thing which is in us in Christ. For I had great joy and consolation in your love, because the hearts <note>original: "σπλάγχνα" — literally 'bowels,' referring to the seat of deep emotions and compassion</note> of the saints have been refreshed by you, brother.

Therefore, though I might be very bold in Christ to command you what is fitting, yet for love’s sake I rather appeal to you—being such a one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ; I appeal to you for my son, whom I have begotten while in my bonds, **Onesimus** <note>The name Onesimus in Greek means "useful" or "profitable," a pun Paul uses in the next sentence.</note>, who once was unprofitable to you, but now is profitable to you and to me, whom I have sent back to you; therefore receive him, that is, my own heart. I wished to keep him with me, that on your behalf he might minister to me in my bonds for the gospel; but without your consent I wanted to do nothing, so that your good deed might not be by compulsion, but voluntary. For perhaps he departed for a while for this reason, that you might receive him forever, no longer as a slave but more than a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.

If then you count me as a partner, receive him as you would me. But if he has wronged you or owes anything, put that on my account. I, Paul, am writing with my own hand. I will repay—not to mention to you that you owe me even your own self besides. Yes, brother, let me have joy from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.

Having confidence in your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say. But meanwhile, also prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted to you.

Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you, as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow laborers. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

<column-break/>

Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.

## To Philemon

Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon the beloved and our coworker, and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our comrade-in-arms, and to the church of your house. Grace be with you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

I thank my God at all times, making mention of you in my prayers, as I hear of your faith and the love that you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints. May the sharing of your faith become manifest through the worship of every good thing that is in you in Jesus Christ. I received much grace and comfort from your love, for the hearts of the saints have found rest through you, brother.

For this reason, I have much boldness in Christ to command you what is worthy; yet for the sake of love, I rather entreat you. Being as I am, Paul the elder, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ, I entreat you for my son whom I fathered in my bonds, **Onesimus**. He was once useless to you, but is now useful to both you and me. I have sent him back to you; and you, receive him, which is to say, my own heart.

I wished to keep him with me so that he might serve me in your stead during my bonds for the gospel. But I did not wish to do anything without your will, so that your goodness might not be as if by necessity, but by will. For perhaps he was separated from you for a time so that you might have him forever; no longer as a servant, but more than a servant—as a beloved brother. Especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.

If you consider me a partner, receive him as you would me. And if he has committed any wrong or owes anything, charge that to me. I, Paul, have written with my own hand: I will compensate you—so as not to tell you that you owe even your own self to me.

Yes, brother, let me be fruitful through you in the Lord; rest my heart in Christ. Trusting in your obedience, I have written to you, because I know that you will do even more than what I say. At the same time, also prepare a lodging for me, for I hope that by your prayers I shall be granted to you. Epaphras, my fellow captive in Christ Jesus, greets you, as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my coworkers. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

But even if I am sacrificed <note>original: "sacrificāto" — reflecting the Greek term for a drink offering or libation</note> upon the work and in service of your faith, I rejoice and am glad with you all. Henceforth, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord! To write the same thing to you is not at all tedious for me, and for you it is a necessary caution. Beware of those dogs, beware of those evil workers, beware of that mutilation <note>original: "ktrtatut'iwn" — Armenian for "cutting" or "shredding," used here to mock the legalistic view of circumcision.</note>. For we are the circumcision, we who worship God in the spirit, and boast in Christ Jesus, and do not boast in the flesh. Although I also have some confidence in the flesh. If anyone exists who looks for confidence in the flesh, I have even more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee. According to zeal, I persecuted the church; according to the righteousness of the law, I was blameless. But whatever was a gain to me, I consider that a loss for the sake of Christ. For his sake, I have let go of everything and count it as loss and refuse <note>original: "kghkank" — meaning excrement or dregs.</note>, so that I may gain Christ.

->**Colossians I.**<-

Paul, apostle of Jesus Christ <note>original: "Jesù XP"</note> by the will of God, and Timothy [the] brother, to those who are in Colossae, who are holy and faithful brothers in Jesus Christ, we wish you grace and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. Giving thanks to God always for you, praying [and] hearing of your faith which you have in Jesus Christ and the affection <note>original: "dilettione"</note> which you have toward the saints, for the hope which is laid up for you in the heavens, which you heard of before in the word of the truth of the gospel which has come to you, even as it did in all the world and grows, and produces fruit even as it did in you on that day when you heard it and knew the grace of God in truth, as you have learned it from Epaphras our most dear fellow-servant <note>original: "conservo"</note> who is a faithful minister of God for you, who has given us to know your affection in the Spirit <note>original: "sp[irit]u"</note>. Therefore we also, from the day that we heard it, do not cease to pray for you and ask that you be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and all spiritual understanding, so that you might be able to walk worthily before God, pleasing God in all things, bearing fruit in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God. Strengthened <note>original: "Confortati"</note> in every virtue according to His divine power to endure all things with patience and joy.

... servants, obey in all things your masters <note>original: "dommano i s... ami"</note>. Not just to be seen or to please men, as physical servants, but as serving Christ with a faithful heart and fear of the eye—but with a simple heart and decorum, fearing God. And whatever you do in word or deed, do it with all your soul as if for God <note>original: "sicome a di... ya"</note> and not for men. Knowing that from God you shall receive the reward of the inheritance... for you serve the Lord Christ. And he who does wrong shall receive according to the wrong he has done; for God does not favor one person over another. **You masters.** Give to your servants what is just and equal, knowing that you also have a Lord in heaven. Persevere in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving to God. Pray to God for us as well, that he might open the door of the word <note>original: "porta del apu... in noi"</note> to us, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in chains <note>original: "pla qua..."</note>, so that I may preach the Gospel. Therefore we pray that I may manifest that Gospel as it is proper for me to speak. Walk with wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time... let your word always be with divine grace and seasoned with salt.

<column-break/>

<note>Left page, Column 2: English (translated from Greek, Colossians 3:22–4:6)</note>

... Slaves, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh, not with eyeservice <note>original: "οφθαλμοδουλείαις", meaning service performed only when watched</note> as men-pleasers, but in sincerity of heart, fearing God. And whatever you do, work from the soul, as to the Lord and not to men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. For you serve the Lord Christ. But he who does wrong will receive back for the wrong he has done, and there is no partiality. **Masters**, provide to your slaves what is just and fair, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven. Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving. Praying at the same time for us also, that God may open for us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also bound, that I may reveal it as I ought to speak. Walk in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the time. Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt.

<note>Left page, Column 3: English (translated from Armenian, Colossians 3:22–4:6)</note>

... Slaves, be obedient in everything to your fleshly masters. Not with eyeservice <note>original: "աչակնութեամբ"</note> as if pleasing men, but with singleness of heart, fearing the Lord. But the unjust shall receive according to his injustice, for there is no respect of persons. **Masters**, provide justice and equality to your servants. Know that you also have a Lord in heaven. Be constant in prayer; be watchful in it with thanksgiving. Make prayer at the same time for us as well, that God may open to us the door of the word to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also bound. Buy back the time <note>original: "գնեցէք զժամանակս", an idiom for making the most of every opportunity</note>. And let your words at all times be seasoned with the salt of grace.

We were gentle in the midst of you, as if a nurse were to cherish her own children. So longing for you, we were pleased to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own souls, because you became beloved to us. For you remember, brothers, our labor and our toil; for working night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you, we preached to you the gospel of God. <note>The following three columns present the opening of the Second Letter to the Thessalonians, traditionally attributed to the Apostle Paul. The text emphasizes endurance through persecution and the promise of divine justice.</note>

To the Thessalonians is sent your epistle: Paul and Silvanus <note>Also known as Silas, a leading member of the early Christian community.</note> and Timothy to the church of Thessalonica in God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ. Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. Brothers, we must always give thanks for you to God as is a worthy thing—because your faith grows exceedingly and the charity of each of you, one for the other, abounds in such a way that we ourselves exalt you <note>original: "innalziamo" — literally "we lift up," meaning to boast or speak highly of.</note> in the churches of God for your patience and for the faith that you have in all the persecutions which you endure as an example of the righteous judgment of God.

<column-break/>

# TO THE THESSALONIANS
## SECOND EPISTLE.

Paul and Silvanus and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ. We are obligated to give thanks to God always concerning you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing abundantly and the love of every single one of you all toward one another is increasing, so that we ourselves boast in you in the churches of God for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are sustaining; a plain indication <note>original: ἔνδειγμα (endeigma) — evidence or proof.</note> of the righteous judgment of God.

<column-break/>

PAUL AND SILVANUS and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and in Lord Jesus Christ: grace be with you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. We are obligated to give thanks to God at all times for you, brothers, as it is indeed worthy; for your faith grows greatly and the love of each and every one of you toward one another abounds. So that we boast of you in the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and in the troubles which you endure; as an example <note>original: յօրինակ (yorinak) — a pattern or model.</note> of the righteous judgment.

---

<column-break/>

...so that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer; since it is righteous for God to repay with affliction those who afflict you, and to give rest to you who are being afflicted, along with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with his powerful angels in a flame of fire, giving vengeance to those who do not know God and to those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus; who will pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his strength, when he comes to be glorified in his saints and to be marveled at in all those who believed—because our testimony to you was believed—on that day. For which we also pray always for you, that our God may make you worthy of the calling and may fulfill...

<column-break/>

...of God, to be worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also bear sufferings. For it is righteous before God to repay your afflicters with affliction; and to you who are afflicted, rest with us at the manifestation <note>original: յայտնութեան (yaytnut‘ean) — revelation or appearing.</note> of our Lord Jesus Christ from heaven with the angels of his power, in a flame of fire, taking vengeance upon those who do not know God, and those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. They shall pay the penalty in eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be wonderful in all his believers; because you believed our testimony to you on that day. For which we also pray at all times for you, that our God may make you worthy of the calling and fill...

<column-break/>

...make that you are worthily excellent in the kingdom of God while enduring tribulations. So that with God there is justice: to return tribulation to those who trouble you: and to you to give rest who are troubled—this will be in the day when Christ will want to come openly from heaven with the angels of his power, with flame of fire which makes vengeance on those who did not know God—who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: which sinners shall bear eternal punishment with perdition—when they shall be cast out from the face of the Lord—and from the glory of his power. When Christ shall come to be glorified in his saints—and to appear wonderfully in all those who believed. In that day he will appear for our testimony upon you—for which thing we always pray for you—that our God deigns to call you in his calling and fulfill his pleasure...

### [Left Folio]

...every will of justice in you, [and the work] of f<unclear>aith</unclear>... with true faith, that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, in this grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ.
We pray you, brothers, for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, for the love of our gathering together in him, that you be not moved from your senses, nor frightened by any spirit, nor by word, nor by epistle as if sent from our part, by which you might say that the day of judgment of the Lord was present there. Let no person deceive you in any way. For [the day] will not come unless first there comes the rebellion <note>original: "el digne..." likely referring to "disdegno" or "disunione," meaning the Great Apostasy.</note> and the man of iniquity is manifested—the Son of Perdition—who opposes and exalts himself above every thing of deity and glory, everything that is seen, in such a way that he will sit in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God. Do you not remember that while I was still with you, I wanted to indicate this to you?

<column-break/>

...every desire for goodness and work of faith in power; so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ. Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to him, not to be quickly shaken in mind, nor alarmed, neither by spirit nor by word nor by letter as if from us, to the effect that the day of the Lord has come. Let no one deceive you in any way. For [it will not come] unless the rebellion <term>apostasia: a falling away or formal defection from the faith</term> comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction, who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, displaying himself as being God. Do you not remember that while I was still with you I was telling you these things?

<column-break/>

...every pleasure of goodness, and the works of faith with power; so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ. I beseech you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our gathering to him, not to be quickly troubled in mind, and not to be terrified, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as if it were from us, as if the day of the Lord has already arrived. Let no one deceive you by any means; for [it will not come] unless the rebellion <note>original: "apstambut'iwnn" — a political or religious revolt.</note> comes first, and the man of lawlessness <note>original: "anorenut'ean" — literally "without-law-ness."</note> is revealed, the son of destruction, the adversary and the one who exalts himself over everything that is called God or worship, until he sits in the temple of God, and shows himself that he is God. Do you not remember that while I was with you, I was saying this to you?

### [Right Folio]
<page-num>244</page-num>

And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only he who now restrains it will do so until he is out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the appearance of his coming; whose coming is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and false wonders, and with all deceit of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved. And for this reason God will send them a working of error, so that they believe the lie, so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but delighted in unrighteousness. But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers beloved by the Lord...

<column-break/>

And now you know that which holds [him], so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness already grows strong; but only until he who now holds [it] is taken out of the midst. And then the lawless one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall destroy with the breath of his mouth, and shall abolish with the manifestation of his coming. Whose coming is according to the influence of Satan, with all power and signs and lying wonders; and with all the deceptions of injustice for those who are perishing; because they did not receive the love of truth that they might live. And for that reason God shall send them the influence of error, that they might believe the lie; that all might be condemned who did not believe the truth, but took pleasure in injustice. But we must give thanks to God at all times for you, brothers beloved of the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth.

<column-break/>

Now you know what restrains that which I said, so that he is manifest in his time; for although the exercise of iniquity already begins, let him hold now that which [is] until he is taken out of the way. Then shall be manifested that wicked one, whom the Lord Jesus Christ will kill with the spirit of his mouth—and destroy him with the appearance of his coming—whose coming is from the deception of Satan with all power—and with signs and lying miracles—and of every... deception—and of iniquity—in those who shall perish—and because they did not receive the charity <note>In this context, "charity" (carita) is used as a translation for the Greek "agape," meaning divine or selfless love.</note> of truth—so that they might be saved—therefore God will send to them the operation of error—so that they believe the lie, so that all those who do not believe the truth—rather they consent to iniquity—may be judged. But we must give thanks to God always for you, beloved brothers—because he [has chosen you] from the first principle of light... through the spirit—in faith of the truth...

# 269

<margin>St. Paul the Apostle</margin>
See to it that you do not refuse the one who spoke so magnanimously upon the earth; we who are in the midst of Him who speaks to us from heaven, whose voice then moved the earth, but now He has promised, saying: "Once more I will move not only the earth, but also the heaven." But this phrase "once more" declares the transformation of movable things, so that those which are immovable may remain. Therefore, since we receive a stable kingdom, let us have grace, through which we may serve God, pleasing Him with fear and reverence. For certainly our God is a smoking fire <note>original: "fumante fuoco," usually translated as "consuming fire"</note> within you.

Chapter 13: Let fraternal charity not be forgotten through hospitality. Through this, some have pleased God, having received angels into their lodging. Remember those in prison, as if you were imprisoned together with them, and those in affliction, as you yourselves dwell in the body. In all things let marriage be held in honor and the bed be immaculate.

<column-break/>

See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking; for if those did not escape when they refused the one who warned them on earth, how much less will we, if we turn away from the one who warns from heaven. His voice shook the earth then; but now he has promised, saying, "Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heaven." This "yet once more" indicates the removal of what is shaken—that is, created things—so that what cannot be shaken may remain. Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us give thanks, by which we may offer acceptable worship to God with reverence and awe; for indeed our God is a consuming fire. Let brotherly love continue. Do not neglect hospitality; for through this, some have unknowingly entertained angels. Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them; those who are being tortured, as being yourselves in the body. Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled.

<column-break/>

Be vigilant regarding this one who speaks. For if they were not able to escape the earthly prophet <note>original: "մարգարէն," literally "prophet," used here for the one giving the command</note> who gave the command on earth... we who have distanced ourselves from the heavenly one: much more let us stand firm on the earth... whose voice shook the earth at that time. And now it is promised and says: "Once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens." "Once more" makes this clear: the transformation of the shaken things as created things, so that the unshakable ones may remain firm. For this reason, since an unshakable kingdom has been received by us, we possess grace, so that by it we may offer service pleasing to God with fear and trembling. For our God is a consuming fire. Let brotherly love be established. Do not forget hospitality, for by it some, unknown to their eyes, received angels. Remember the captives as if you were bound with them; the tormented as if you yourselves were in the body. Honorable is marriage in every way, and holy are the beds.

Do not linger in various and foreign-sounding <note>original: "օտարաձայնս," meaning strange or alien voices/teachings</note> doctrines. <column-break/>

Therefore God will judge the fornicators and adulterers. Let your customs be without avarice: being content with present things, for He said, "I will not release nor abandon you," so that we may say confidently: "The Lord is my helper, I will not fear what man may do to me." Remember your predecessors <note>original: "antecessori," likely referring to bishops or leaders</note> by whom the word of God was spoken to you; considering the exit <note>original: "l'exito," meaning the outcome or end</note> of their conversation, follow their faith. Through varied and strange doctrines... certainly it is an excellent thing to stabilize the heart with grace, not with foods, which have not benefited those who lived in that manner in any way. We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle have no power to eat. ### [Folio 319r]

And the angel said to me: "Why did you marvel? I will tell you the **mystery** <note>original: "μυστήριον" (mystērion); here meaning a hidden truth now revealed</note> of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns. The beast that you saw **was, and is not**, and is about to rise from the **abyss** <term>abyss: "ἀβύσσου" (abyssou), the bottomless pit or primordial void</term>, and goes to destruction. And those dwelling on the earth, whose names have not been written in the **book of life** from the foundation of the world, will marvel when they see the beast, because it was, and is not, and will be present. 

Here is the mind that has wisdom: The seven heads are **seven mountains** where the woman sits upon them. And they are seven kings; five have fallen, and one is, the other has not yet come, and when he comes, he must remain for a little while. And the beast that was and is not, he himself is the eighth, and is of the seven, and goes to destruction. And the ten horns which you saw are **ten kings**, who have not yet received a kingdom, but they receive authority as kings for one hour with the beast. These have one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast. These will make war with the **Lamb**, and the Lamb will conquer them, because he is **Lord of lords and King of kings**, and those with him are called and chosen and faithful." And he says to me: "The waters which you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues."

And the angel said to me: "Why did you wonder? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has seven heads and ten horns. And the beast which you saw, which **was and is not**, and is prepared to come up from the abyss <note>Armenian: "յանդնդոց" (yandndots), meaning from the deeps or the pit</note> and to go into destruction. And all the inhabitants of the earth will wonder, whose names are not written in the book of life from the creation of the world, seeing the beast which was and is not, and is near. 

Here is the mind that has wisdom: the seven heads are **seven mountains** where the woman sat upon them. And there are seven kings; five have fallen, and one is, and the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain for a short time. And the beast that was and is not, he is the eighth, and is from the seven, and is to go to destruction. And the ten horns which you saw are **ten kings** who have not yet received the kingdom; but they take authority as kings for one hour with the beast. These have one will, and they give their strength and authority to the beast. These war against the **Lamb** <note>Armenian: "գառինն" (garrinn), referring to Jesus Christ as the sacrificial Lamb of God</note>, and the Lamb shall conquer them, for he is the Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with him are called and chosen and faithful."
